section: Cabinet system, Cabinet committees, collective and individual responsibility; Attorney General of India
subsections: AG vs Solicitor General - legal status
Cabinet dominance - single-party vs coalition eras

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a qualification for appointment as the Attorney General of India?
o: Having been a High Court advocate for ten years
Being a citizen of India
Having been a High Court Judge for five years
Having served as a Member of Parliament for five years
accepted.x: The qualifications include Indian citizenship, five years as a High Court Judge, ten years as a High Court advocate, or being an eminent jurist. Prior membership of Parliament is not prescribed.
accepted.tq: Find the option that substitutes a political qualification for a legal qualification.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the resignation of the Attorney General of India is correct?
o: The Attorney General resigns by convention when the government changes.
The Attorney General must resign whenever the Lok Sabha is dissolved.
The Constitution requires resignation at the end of every financial year.
The Attorney General can resign only after approval by the Supreme Court.
accepted.x: Although the Constitution does not fix the Attorney General’s term, the Attorney General conventionally resigns when the government changes.
accepted.tq: Distinguish constitutional provisions from conventions governing office-holding.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a duty of the Attorney General of India?
o: Advising the Government of India on legal matters
Appearing for the Government of India in the Supreme Court
Appearing in references made under Article 143
Presiding over joint sittings of Parliament
accepted.x: The Attorney General advises the Government of India, appears for it in the Supreme Court, and appears in Article 143 references. The Attorney General does not preside over joint sittings of Parliament.
accepted.tq: Reject the option assigning a parliamentary presiding function to the chief law officer.

accepted.s: Under Article 88 of the Constitution, the Attorney General of India has the right to:
o: Dissolve either House of Parliament with the President’s approval
Participate only in proceedings of the Rajya Sabha
Speak in either House, joint sittings and parliamentary committees without the right to vote
Vote in both Houses of Parliament and their committees
accepted.x: Article 88 permits the Attorney General to speak and participate in either House, joint sittings and parliamentary committees, but does not confer a right to vote.
accepted.tq: Test the confusable distinction between participation and voting.

accepted.s: The parliamentary privileges available to the Attorney General are specifically associated with:
o: Article 143
Article 105(4)
Article 177
Article 165
accepted.x: The Attorney General enjoys the privileges of a Member of Parliament under Article 105(4), even though the Attorney General is not a Member of Parliament.
accepted.tq: Match the office-related privilege with its constitutional article.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the professional limitations of the Attorney General of India:
1. The office is not a full-time office.
2. The Attorney General may undertake private practice.
3. The Attorney General may advise or brief against the Government of India in private practice.
4. The Attorney General may become a company director without permission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 4 only
accepted.x: The office is not full-time and private practice is permitted. However, the Attorney General cannot advise or brief against the Government of India and cannot become a company director without permission.
accepted.tq: Use the prohibited activities to eliminate overbroad statements.

accepted.s: Which one of the following activities is prohibited to the Attorney General of India?
o: Defending an accused person in a criminal case
Speaking in a parliamentary committee without voting
Advising the Government of India on legal matters
Appearing in the Supreme Court for the Government of India
accepted.x: The Attorney General cannot defend accused persons in criminal cases. Advising the Union Government, appearing in the Supreme Court for it and speaking in committees are recognised functions or rights.
accepted.tq: Identify the professional restriction hidden among ordinary constitutional functions.

accepted.s: Who was the first Attorney General of India?
o: M.C. Setalvad
C.K. Daphtary
K. Parasaran
Niren De
accepted.x: M.C. Setalvad was the first Attorney General of India. C.K. Daphtary was the first Solicitor General.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the first holders of two closely related law offices.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the legal status of the Attorney General and the Solicitor General of India?
o: The Attorney General’s office is constitutional, whereas the Solicitor General’s office is statutory.
The Attorney General’s office is statutory, whereas the Solicitor General’s office is constitutional.
Both offices are constitutional offices under Article 76.
Both offices are created only by executive convention.
accepted.x: The Attorney General is a constitutional office under Article 76. The Solicitor General is a statutory office and is not mentioned in the Constitution.
accepted.tq: Separate constitutional and statutory offices before comparing their functions.
accepted.sec: AG vs Solicitor General - legal status

accepted.s: With reference to the term of office of the Attorney General and the Solicitor General, which one of the following is correct?
o: The Attorney General has no fixed term, whereas the Solicitor General has a term of three years.
The Attorney General has a term of three years, whereas the Solicitor General has no fixed term.
Both have a constitutionally fixed term of three years.
Both offices continue only until the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
accepted.x: The Constitution does not fix the Attorney General’s term. The Solicitor General’s term is three years.
accepted.tq: Compare the tenure rules instead of assuming identical treatment for the two law officers.
accepted.sec: AG vs Solicitor General - legal status

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the advice given by the Attorney General from the role of the Solicitor General?
o: The Attorney General advises the Government of India, whereas the Solicitor General only appears in courts.
The Solicitor General advises the Government of India, whereas the Attorney General only appears in courts.
Both advise the Government of India on all legal matters.
Neither officer may appear in courts on behalf of the Government of India.
accepted.x: The Attorney General advises the Government of India on legal matters. The Solicitor General’s role, as distinguished here, is limited to appearing in courts and does not include giving such advice.
accepted.tq: Separate advisory responsibility from courtroom representation.
accepted.sec: AG vs Solicitor General - legal status

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the appointment of the Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General?
o: They are recommended by the Supreme Court and appointed by the Chief Justice of India.
They are recommended by the Election Commission and appointed by Parliament.
They are recommended by the Attorney General and appointed by the Governor.
They are recommended by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet and appointed by the President.
accepted.x: The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet recommends the Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General, and the President appoints them.
accepted.tq: Ask which authority performs the recommendation and appointment functions.
accepted.sec: AG vs Solicitor General - legal status

accepted.s: The State-level counterpart of the Attorney General of India is the:
o: State Solicitor General, appointed by the Chief Minister
Legal Secretary, appointed by the President
Public Prosecutor, appointed by the High Court
Advocate General, appointed by the Governor
accepted.x: The Advocate General is the counterpart of the Attorney General at the State level. The Advocate General is appointed by the Governor under Article 165.
accepted.tq: Apply the Union–State counterpart method to constitutional law officers.
accepted.sec: AG vs Solicitor General - legal status

accepted.s: The Advocate General of a State has the right to speak in the State Legislature under:
o: Article 165
Article 88
Article 76
Article 177
accepted.x: Article 177 gives the Advocate General the right to speak and participate in the proceedings of the State Legislature, without a right to vote. Article 165 relates to the office itself.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the article creating the office from the article conferring legislative participation.
accepted.sec: AG vs Solicitor General - legal status

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the position of the Union Cabinet during single-party majority eras in India?
o: Collective responsibility is constitutionally suspended during a majority government.
Coalition coordination committees determine all Cabinet decisions.
Parliament invariably exercises complete control over the Cabinet.
The Prime Minister and Cabinet generally exercise strong dominance over Parliament.
accepted.x: During single-party majority eras, the Prime Minister and Cabinet generally dominate Parliament, leading to the criticism that the system may resemble a ‘cabinet dictatorship’.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a political tendency from a formal constitutional rule.
accepted.sec: Cabinet dominance - single-party vs coalition eras

accepted.s: The coalition era referred to in the context of Cabinet functioning broadly covers:
accepted.x: The coalition era identified here is the period from 1989 to 2014. During this period, coordination committees and allies’ demands affected Cabinet cohesion and collective responsibility.
accepted.tq: Test the exact beginning and end years of the political phase.
accepted.sec: Cabinet dominance - single-party vs coalition eras

accepted.s: Why did coalition politics tend to weaken Cabinet cohesion and collective responsibility during 1989–2014?
o: Because coordination committees and the demands of alliance partners influenced government functioning
Because the President directly exercised all Cabinet powers
Because Parliament ceased to examine government expenditure
Because the Constitution abolished the office of the Prime Minister during coalition governments
accepted.x: Coalition governments had to accommodate coordination committees and the demands of alliance partners. This often weakened Cabinet cohesion and the effective operation of collective responsibility.
accepted.tq: Connect the political condition with its institutional consequence.
accepted.sec: Cabinet dominance - single-party vs coalition eras

accepted.s: Which one of the following is regarded as a criticism of excessive concentration of power in the Prime Minister’s Office and Cabinet committees?
o: It strengthens independent decision-making by every Cabinet minister.
It dilutes collective decision-making by the Cabinet as a whole.
It transfers all legislative privileges to the Attorney General.
It makes coalition coordination committees constitutionally mandatory.
accepted.x: Excessive concentration of power in the PMO and Cabinet committees is criticised for diluting collective Cabinet decision-making.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional consequence of centralisation within the executive.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Shadow Cabinet:
1. The Shadow Cabinet is associated with the United Kingdom.
2. India has a formal constitutional counterpart of the Shadow Cabinet.
Which of the statements given above is correct?
o: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
accepted.x: The Shadow Cabinet is a feature associated with the United Kingdom. India has no formal counterpart of the Shadow Cabinet.
accepted.tq: Test the common comparative-politics assumption that similar parliamentary systems have identical institutions.

accepted.s: In July 2026, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved the construction of the third and fourth railway lines on which section?
o: Vijayawada–Gudur section
Visakhapatnam–Kottavalasa section
Ballari–Guntakal section
Guntakal–Renigunta section
accepted.x: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved the third and fourth railway lines on the Ballari–Guntakal section at a cost of Rs 1,264 crore.
accepted.tq: Use the location and project-number combination to identify the correct current-affairs item.

accepted.s: The cost approved for the third and fourth railway lines on the Ballari–Guntakal section was:
o: Rs 1,426 crore
Rs 1,624 crore
Rs 1,126 crore
Rs 1,264 crore
accepted.x: The approved cost of the third and fourth railway lines on the Ballari–Guntakal section was Rs 1,264 crore.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among closely spaced numerical values.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to recent senior administrative appointments?
o: T.V. Somanathan — extension up to 22 August 2027
Govind Mohan — one-year extension as Cabinet Secretary
T.V. Somanathan — one-year extension as Cabinet Secretary
G. Sai Prasad — appointment as Union Home Secretary
accepted.x: The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet approved a one-year extension for Cabinet Secretary Dr. T.V. Somanathan. Govind Mohan’s tenure as Home Secretary was extended up to 22 August 2027, while G. Sai Prasad became Andhra Pradesh Chief Secretary.
accepted.tq: Match each officer with the correct office and tenure detail.

accepted.s: The Cabinet papers relating to the caste-census decision were exempted from disclosure under which provision of the Right to Information Act?
o: Section 8(1)(i)
Section 10(2)(i)
Section 9(1)(b)
Section 8(1)(a)
accepted.x: The Cabinet papers relating to the caste-census decision were held exempt under Section 8(1)(i) of the Right to Information Act.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact statutory provision rather than the broader subject of exemption.

accepted.s: Who is regarded as the State equivalent of the Cabinet Secretary?
o: The Chief Secretary
The State Election Commissioner
The State Public Prosecutor
The Advocate General
accepted.x: The Chief Secretary is regarded as the State equivalent of the Cabinet Secretary. G. Sai Prasad took charge as Andhra Pradesh Chief Secretary in February 2026.
accepted.tq: Apply the Union–State administrative equivalent pairing.

accepted.s: Who took charge as the Chief Secretary of Andhra Pradesh in February 2026?
o: G. Sai Prasad
C.K. Daphtary
T.V. Somanathan
Govind Mohan
accepted.x: G. Sai Prasad took charge as the Chief Secretary of Andhra Pradesh in February 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the State appointment from the Union-level administrative appointments.
